neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that on 25.11.2003, the accused's husband returned home from a clinic and found a servant, aged 13 years, weeping. Upon entering the house, he discovered his daughter-in-law dead and his wife unconscious. The accused, who was the step mother-in-law of the deceased, had a domestic dispute with the deceased. The servant, who worked with the family, identified the accused persons in court. The servant stated that one accused caught the deceased and another attacked her with a knife 3-4 times. The incident occurred in the courtyard, with the accused present in the passage. The accused threatened the servant not to disclose the incident. The accused fled after the assault, and one of them took the servant to the terrace and instructed him to falsely accuse thieves. The prosecution examined 32 witnesses, and the trial court convicted all the accused under Section 302 r/w Section 34 and Section 1208, IPC. The High Court confirmed the conviction.

His statement that accused no. 2 attacked the deceased with a knife was corroborated by the recovery of the knife from accused no. 2. The court also noted that accused no. 1 had a scuffle with the deceased, as evidenced by her hair being found in her grip during investigation.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that accused no. 1 hired contract killers accused no. 2 and 4 to kill her daughter-in-law (deceased) due to domestic disputes. The child witness PW-21, who was brought up by accused no. 1, provided testimony that accused no. 2 and 4 attacked the deceased with a knife, and the knife was recovered from accused no. 2. The prosecution also highlighted the motive of accused no. 1 to hinder the marriage of her son.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that accused no. 3 (Mahesh) did not play any role in the crime, as there was no evidence of his involvement, no weapon or property connected with the crime was seized from him, and he was merely seen standing outside the house. The defence also questioned the reliability of the child witness PW-21, suggesting he might have been tutored by the police.

quotes.text: The learned counsel for the appellants forcefully attacked the conviction of the other accused viz. Mahesh, Chandra Prakash and Devendra Kumar, who admittedly were not known to the child witness Anil Kumar.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that common intention and conspiracy are matters of inference, and if any benefit of doubt arises, it must go to the accused. The Court also emphasized the need for corroboration of the testimony of a child witness in cases where the accused are strangers to the witness.

quotes.text: It is settled law that common intention and conspiracy are matters of inference and if while drawing an inference any benefit of doubt creeps in, it must go to the accused.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed as the Court upheld the conviction of accused no. 1, 2, and 4 under Section 302 r/w Section 34 and 1208 of the IPC, considering the evidence of the child witness and the corroborating knife recovery. Accused no. 3 was acquitted due to lack of evidence of his involvement.

quotes.text: The trial court convicted all the accused under Section 302 r/w Section 34 and Section 1208, IPC. The High Court confirmed the conviction. The instant appeal was filed challenging the order of the High Court.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The Court considered that the child witness PW-21 was brought up by accused no. 1, who took care of him, sent him to school, and provided him with food and residence, which made it unlikely for him to falsely implicate anyone.

quotes.text: He was brought to the house by accused no.1 who apparently took care of him and sent to school and gave him food and residence. He had no grouse against her neither any ulterior motive in identifying the accused, who were not acquainted to him.

judicial_aggravating_factors.value: The Court noted that accused no. 2 and 4 had a single mission to kill the deceased, and there was no evidence of their previous animosity with the deceased, indicating a premeditated act.

quotes.text: It is obvious that accused nos. 2 and 4 did not enter the house to commit a robbery and had a single mission, namely, to kill the deceased. There was no evidence that they had any previous animosity with the deceased and appeared to have acted as contract killers.

other_sentence_order.value: The Court acquitted accused no. 3 and discharged his bail bonds and sureties. It also emphasized the need for corroboration of child witness testimony and the importance of fair identification procedures.

quotes.text: The accused no. 3 is innocent and the conviction against him is set aside. His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged.
